summary:
**FIRELENS** is a web platform (also available as a Windows desktop app) that detects and displays wildfires on an interactive 3D globe, built with CesiumJS, FastAPI and Python.

**What I developed:** a system that harmonizes active-fire data from the NASA MODIS and VIIRS satellites (via NASA FIRMS) into a single model and groups detections into *fire events*. It offers filters, a historical fire calendar, fire perimeters, alert rules, and a fire-danger forecast based on weather (Open-Meteo) and vegetation (Sentinel-2 NDVI).

**How it addresses the challenge:** it unifies heterogeneous satellite sources and makes them easy to understand: automatic hourly updates, searchable history by country or area, and an offline demo mode. It works without API keys or complex installation.

**Why it matters:** wildfires threaten lives, ecosystems and the climate. Scattered, technical data slows response; FIRELENS makes it accessible, visual and open, supporting early detection, prevention and better decision-making.
details:
Project Details: FIRELENS

What it does and how it works

FIRELENS shows wildfires on a 3D virtual Earth. It pulls active-fire detections from NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellites (through NASA FIRMS) and harmonizes them into one common data model. It then groups nearby detections into fire events, so users see incidents instead of thousands of separate points.

  • Live mode: the last days of global data load on first start and refresh every hour.
  • History mode: users pick a day or range, or click or drag across a calendar heatmap. If that period isn't loaded for the area in view, FIRELENS fetches it from NASA's archive automatically.
  • Analysis: filters by time, area and confidence, fire perimeters, alert rules, and a fire-danger forecast built from weather (Open-Meteo) and vegetation (Copernicus Sentinel-2 NDVI).
  • Offline demo mode: synthetic data lets every screen be explored without internet.

Benefits

  • Satellite fire data is normally scattered across formats and hard to read. FIRELENS makes it visual and searchable.
  • It works with no API keys and no installation. Optional keys unlock historical archives and satellite readings per fire.
  • It runs several ways: online on Railway, as a Windows app, or from source.

Expected impact

FIRELENS supports early awareness, monitoring and prevention. Researchers, emergency teams, journalists and the public can see where fires are burning and where conditions raise the risk, using open data. Better visibility helps people make faster, better-informed decisions.

Tools and technologies

  • Backend: Python 3.11+, FastAPI and Uvicorn, with SQLite for storage.
  • Frontend: a Node 20+ and Vite web app using CesiumJS for the 3D globe.
  • Data sources: NASA FIRMS (MODIS and VIIRS), Open-Meteo, Copernicus Sentinel-2.
  • Packaging and deployment: Docker and Railway for the website and API in one container, PyInstaller for the Windows executable, and Inno Setup for the installer.
  • Testing: pytest, with respx for mocking HTTP calls.

What is creative about it

  • It harmonizes two different satellite sensors into a single model.
  • It turns raw detections into fire events and tells their story over time on a calendar heatmap.
  • It combines live detection, history and a danger forecast in one tool.
  • Missing history is loaded automatically as the user explores.
  • It ships as a double-click Windows app with a built-in demo mode.

Factors we considered

  • Accessibility: it needs no technical setup, no accounts and no keys to get started.
  • Data quality: MODIS and VIIRS differ in resolution and confidence, so there is a low-confidence switch, and demo and live databases never mix.
  • Performance and limits: archive loads are capped by view size and date range, and NASA's request limits shape how much loads at once.
  • Reliability: hourly refresh, offline fallback, and local storage that the user can delete to start fresh.
  • Maintainability: full documentation covering architecture, API, data and roadmap.
